system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Stability: Markets, US–China Truce, and Regional Wars
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where a cautious US–China engagement sits alongside persistent regional wars and a sharp repricing of risk across financial markets. Policy choices (trade truce, tariffs, export‑ban talk) and technological leverage (chips, rare earths, AI) are being used as tools of statecraft while central banks and bond markets react to faster-than-expected tightening, amplifying economic spillovers. Simultaneously, active kinetic conflicts (Ukraine, Iran-linked strikes, Yemen, Ethiopia) and allied security anxieties (NATO, Baltic, Black Sea) keep supply, energy and diplomatic channels unstable, making short-term cooperation brittle and contingent on domestic politics.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and major power interactions (US, China, Russia, EU, Middle East actors), interstate alliances and institutions (NATO, G20, UN, trade agreements), global financial markets and central banks, energy and commodity flows, critical technology and supply chains (chips, rare earths, AI), and active regional conflicts and insurgencies.
system_description.super_system: The planetary political-economic system of globalization — an integrated international order of states, markets, transnational institutions and infrastructure.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial/monetary subsystem (sovereign debt, bond markets, central banks)
Global energy and commodity subsystem (oil, gas, diesel, shipping chokepoints)
High-tech industrial-supply chains (semiconductors, AI hardware, rare earths)
Alliance and security subsystem (NATO, regional security architectures, military deployments)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine high-intensity war
variables.description: A sustained, high-intensity military confrontation between Russia and Ukraine, with Western military and economic support for Kyiv progressively reshaping battlefield dynamics and alliance burden-sharing.

variables.name: U.S.-China strategic competition
variables.description: A broad geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China over trade, technology (AI, chips, data), and regional security (including Taiwan), characterised by episodic diplomacy, targeted controls, and incremental decoupling.

variables.name: Iran-led regional confrontation and diplomacy
variables.description: An oscillating confrontation between Iran and a U.S.-aligned set of states and proxies, alternating between military escalation and intermittent negotiations that are reshaping regional alignments and the scope of external intervention.

variables.name: Global bond-market and monetary shock
variables.description: A widespread repricing of fixed-income markets led by surging U.S. Treasury yields and tighter central bank stances, shifting global capital flows, borrowing costs and political-economic pressures across advanced and emerging economies.

variables.name: Global fuel and energy-market stress
variables.description: Acute volatility and supply-security stresses in global oil and fuel markets—driven by supply shocks, shipping disruptions and debated export restrictions—that are prompting policy interventions and raising costs for producers and consumers.
